- BP, pulse rate and rhythm: Not recorded.

Focused joint findings (left elbow – video assessment)
  • Visible localized swelling around olecranon  
  • Area warmer than adjacent skin; mild tenderness adjacent to tip; full range of movement maintained  
  • Overlying skin noted mildly dry; no erythema concerning for septic arthritis at time of review  

Investigations (as indicated)

- Ordered: Blood panel to include inflammatory markers (e.g., ESR/CRP), infection screen, rheumatologic antibodies, serum uric acid (gout screen)  
- Fasting BGL and lipids: Not ordered/recorded.  
- Cervical screening, STI screen, mammogram, other pathology: Not applicable / not discussed.  

Management Plan

- Commence NSAID therapy: Ibuprofen 400 mg orally twice daily with food; cease if gastrointestinal side effects occur.  
- Pathology request form to be mailed to patient; patient to attend phlebotomy for ordered blood tests promptly.  
- Review results and clinical progress in approximately 6 days via video or face-to-face appointment per patient preference.  
- Red flag education: Seek urgent review if elbow becomes very red, increasingly painful, rapidly enlarges, or systemic symptoms develop (possible septic arthritis).  
- No immediate need for imaging or specialist referral at this stage; reassess after blood results.
